PEGylation can extend nanoparticle circulation half-life to over 40 hours by reducing opsonization and RES clearance.
Optimal PEG surface coverage for PLA, PLGA, and polycaprolactone nanoparticles is about 5 wt%, with 5–7 mol% PEG providing stable liposome formulations.
PEG forms a mushroom-like structure at low surface density and a brush-like conformation at higher densities, affecting stealth efficiency.
PEGylated liposomes such as Doxil are clinically approved for metastatic breast cancer, ovarian cancer, and Kaposi sarcoma treatment.
Repeated injection of PEGylated liposomes can induce anti-PEG IgM antibodies, causing accelerated blood clearance mediated by splenic B cells.
Poly(2-ethyl-2-oxazoline) and poly(hydroxyethyl-L-asparagine) are promising PEG alternatives with comparable stealth effects and better biodegradability.
Polybetaines, including sulfobetaine and carboxybetaine, reduce nonspecific protein adsorption and bacterial adhesion due to strong hydration via electrostatic interactions.
Polyglycerols provide antifouling effects comparable to PEG but with less susceptibility to oxidation and thermal stress.
pH-sensitive hydrazone linkers enable PEG detachment in acidic tumor microenvironments (pH ~5–6), exposing cell-adhesive peptides to enhance uptake.
Matrix metalloproteinase (MMP)-sensitive peptide linkers allow enzymatic cleavage of PEG in tumors, improving cellular internalization and gene delivery.
PEGylation can reduce intracellular delivery efficiency by interfering with endosomal escape and cellular uptake of nanoparticles.
Polysaccharide coatings like chitosan can improve cellular uptake in acidic tumor environments due to their positive charge.
Nanoparticle size inversely correlates with drug release rate due to membrane curvature effects on phospholipid permeability.
Ultrasound can be used as an external stimulus to trigger drug release from nanoparticles.
Biomimetic coatings, such as cell membrane camouflaging and CD47 functionalization, help nanoparticles evade immune detection by mimicking 'self' signals.
